key_insight: A 4D diffusion-based generative model learns continuous spatiotemporal brain anatomy changes from temporally sparse longitudinal scans, enabling realistic interpolation and simulation of neurodegenerative progression.
problem_solved: Sparse follow-up scans in longitudinal neuroimaging make it hard to model continuous disease progression at the subject level; this approach fills temporal gaps and captures smooth anatomical trajectories.
method: Formulate a 4D (3D space + time) generative diffusion model that encodes and decodes spatiotemporal brain anatomy rather than isolated timepoints.
Train the model to learn smooth temporal dynamics from population-level longitudinal examples, enabling interpolation/extrapolation between few observed follow-ups.
Incorporate anatomy-aware constraints and temporal conditioning (e.g., baseline anatomy, time offsets) to preserve structural plausibility and subject-specific progression.
impact: Provides practitioners a tool to augment sparse longitudinal datasets, generate plausible intermediate scans, and improve downstream tasks (progression prediction, biomarker discovery) without requiring dense follow-up data.
visual_elements: Timeline diagram: sparse observed MRI timepoints vs. continuous interpolated trajectory produced by the 4D model.
Model schematic: encoder/decoder diffusion pipeline highlighting 3D spatial + time dimension and temporal conditioning inputs.
Before/after brain maps: example morphometric changes or simulated intermediate scans illustrating disease progression.
Evaluation charts: qualitative realism (visual examples) and quantitative metrics (interpolation fidelity, preserved anatomy) as compact bar/line plots.
paper_title: Generative Modeling of Neurodegenerative Brain Anatomy with 4D Longitudinal Diffusion Model
paper_authors: Nivetha Jayakumar, Swakshar Deb, Bahram Jafrasteh, Qingyu Zhao, Miaomiao Zhang
